why: marks go, words stay
spoken: Plan. first, check the traps. then count them.

why: code is never read out
spoken: Run this: There is a code block here. Then wait.

why: a fence left open is still not read out
spoken: Here: There is a code block here.

why: a link is its words, a bare URL is "a link"
spoken: See the guide or a link.

why: a picture is said to be one
spoken: a picture: a heron by the pier.

why: a persona's citation is where it came from
text: Urchins graze kelp [urchin-barrens.pdf, p. 4: "grazing fronts move"] in winter.
spoken: Urchins graze kelp (from urchin barrens) in winter.

why: a citation without a page
nothing to say is nothing
a rule is nothing
an action in asterisks is its words
an underscore inside a word is not emphasis
underscores around words are
bold in underscores
bold in underscores across a sentence end is still bold
bold in asterisks across a sentence end too
struck words are read
inline code keeps its words
a numbered list
text:
1. Pack the bag.
2. Lock the door
spoken: Pack the bag. Lock the door.

why: a quote
a table is its cells
a line that ends without punctuation still ends a sentence
an ellipsis is left as written
a vocal tag is the speech engine's, never touched
a smile is not a link
text: Nice to see you :) How was the ferry? It ran late.
spoken: Nice to see you :) How was the ferry? It ran late.

why: spacing is one space
a script without spaces ends a sentence at its own mark
and its full-width marks end a line as a full stop does
